doc.notes: A node-only fixture: it lives outside the shipped tracks dir, is read only by web/tools/test-ballreturn.mjs (which looks definitions up in the shipped tracks dir first, then in this fixtures dir), and is never served to the browser. Three feeders land on one trunk: rc-run and cc-run land at one trunk station, lc-run lands at the trunk head. Route 0 (cc-run, corner pocket 0) enters inside the wpa_generic_9ft corner leg, so furnitureClearance refuses the whole track [V20] — the entry has 0.00 mm of clear runway above it, 57.15 mm short of the one ball diameter the landing law seats an arriving ball in, and the run below the entry stands inside the leg as well. A clear entry would need about 170 mm of plan travel, beyond what the entry law's cup radius admits, and every generic-bed corner carries the same leg, so the fixture cannot be re-sited clear inside the shipped tracks dir; it was relocated here instead (#749). The node arms keep reading it by name as the three-feeder topology pin; the shipped-dir census reads it only as its negative control. Geometry values are TEST reads chosen from the table's own dimensions with stated clearances; nothing here is a claim about any real slide.

PROXY: the kernel default class (params.rs ClothPreset::default, u_r 0.010 — Waldron stimpmeter roll-out, a first-hand cloth measurement) stands in for the unmeasured steel-wire class. On the twin rail the effective coefficient is (7/5)(r/ρ)·u_r = 1.4 × 1.322 × 0.010 = 0.0185 (track.js resistCoeff); drain margin at the shallowest edge: sin θ 0.0436 vs 0.0185.

research.md R5 / the brief's 'inelastic arrival' and the owner's 「一个接一个堆」: arriving balls share a common velocity with the group they touch, the tray wall is infinite mass. A modelling decision, NOT a measurement — no ball-on-ball impact in a return tray has been captured in this repo; a measured e would enter through this block and a runtime law change (spec §7).
